title: Placeholder-to-pitch-deck concept art for a solo dev: what worked and what didn't
author: Orbes-technologies
selftext:
Solo devs hit the "I need 30 concept images to pitch this, and I can't draw" wall, and I've been there. The biggest fix was locking the camera and lens words early ("isometric, 3/4 top-down"). Before that, none of my tiles lined up. Next was silhouettes: at thumbnail size they read far better than detail, so I now prompt for a strong silhouette on a flat background.

  
The mindset shift: generated art is my reference and pitch layer, not final assets. I treat it as a mood board an artist can beat. And I keep a prompt log per biome (these four tiles are swamp, desert ruin, ice cave, mushroom forest), so I can regenerate consistently weeks later.

  
What's your pipeline for keeping style consistent across a pitch?
